milestone:
M6: analytics dashboards, weekly reviews and cycle reviews with next-cycle generation, in 63 small PRs across 12 tracks. This revision fixes all 22 of the critic's problems. It was re-checked against origin/main 939afc2, which adds #91 (m3/27 ownerToday and the program fixture route), #96 (m2x/02 desk-rules and scripts/layout-rules.test.ts), #97 (m3/22 volume) and #98 (m4/04 timers) to 82fa9d3. Migrations still end at 0015_coaching_memory. The plan builds on the M2 onboarding, M2X, M3, M4 and M5 plans and names their slices by real id.

Build order:
1. A pure, isomorphic analytics engine in src/lib/domain/analytics.
   - Every period is made of complete weeks, and the week in progress is shown apart, compared with the same days of last week.
   - Only periods.ts and types.ts may reach the browser. One shared import walker proves it.
2. PRD §5 rules as data, then the review snapshot, weekly composition, next-week edit ops, cycle evaluation, cycle directives with late-start dates, and a next-block generator derived from M3's exported STAGES. All of this lives in the server-only domain/programming package.
3. Fact queries that count only completed, undeleted workouts, loaded once per request, with shared unit formatting. Muscle-group targets come from the input that generated each block. Then the dashboard services.
4. A hand-built chart kit. The SVG draws only lines and areas, and every mark that needs a pixel size is an HTML box. Chart bodies load through one SSR-guarded registry.
5. The Progress tab and exercise detail, server-rendered view by view, with offline, failed-load and no-JS states and a byte allowance for every slice. None of it waits on M5.
6. Two migration slots after M5's coach-explain: reviews-db (reviews are superseded, never overwritten, and earlier rows stay valid) and analytics-explain (two-year service time, page-load time and page-data size).
7. Review services on M5's proposal lifecycle:
   - provenance is stored in evidence.source
   - the latest revision is always followed
   - decisions made late keep only the changes still ahead
   - a next_cycle proposal is never applied from the inbox
8. A read-only coach write-up behind its own long-running endpoint. Its thread is kept out of Recent conversations, and leaving the page never cancels it.
9. Review screens, bridge-week states, entry points, perf gates, two journeys and two docs slices.

PERIODS AND THE WEEK IN PROGRESS (problem 6). periods.ts periodWindow(today, period, firstActivityOn) returns:
- weeks: the period's complete Monday–Sunday weeks, ending the Sunday before today's week
- inProgress: today's week, from Monday to today, never part of weeks
- previous: as many complete weeks, ending the day before; null for 'all'
- bucket: week, or month once 'all' spans more than 104 weeks
Rules:
- trend points, period totals, averages, deltas and comparisons use complete weeks only, so 11 weeks and 3 days are never compared with 12 full weeks, and a Wednesday never looks like a decline
- the week in progress is shown apart, as 'This week so far: 6,200 kg · 5,900 kg by Wednesday last week', a like-for-like comparison through sameDaysLastWeek
- charts mark it: a dashed ring labelled 'so far' on lines, an outlined column on bars
- events (PRs, a race, a best effort) are dated and listed whenever they happen, the week in progress included
- a new owner in their first week sees only the in-progress week, with dated availability
Tested with today on a Wednesday in periods, series, metric-catalogue and the dashboard services.

TREND VERSUS NOISE (trend.ts; ADR proposed in trend-classifier, accepted in docs-m6-architecture).
The method:
- Theil–Sen slope with a median intercept
- Mann–Kendall two-sided p: exact through Mahonian dynamic programming for n ≤ 20 without ties, otherwise the normal approximation with tie and continuity corrections
- noise = 1.4826 × the MAD of the residuals
A real trend needs:
- at least 6 points spanning at least 21 days
- p < 0.05
- |slope × span| ≥ max(the metric's minimal practical change, 2 × noise)
Outliers beyond 3 robust SD are flagged, never removed. Points flagged inProgress are never used. Error rates are proven on 200 seeded series per case.
VERDICT WINDOW: trendWindow(period) is the period's complete weeks when the period is 12w or longer, and the last 12 complete weeks for 4w. When the two differ, each tile says 'Trend over the last 12 weeks'.

MUSCLE-GROUP TARGETS (problem 5). A week stores only {rpeCap, volumeFactor, loadStep, runVolumeFactor}. services/analytics/targets.ts (analytics-facts) is the one source of targets.
Finding the range:
- A week's block is judged by the input that generated it. That is the input_snapshot of the lowest-numbered version of the program that has a generator and holds that block lineage as a planned block: v1 for M3's first block, and planBlock's version for blocks M6 plans (next-block-store stores the generator and the input).
- The range is volume.ts's new export hardSetBand(chooseSplit(input, 1), input.nutritionPhase). The split's style needs no day count. The band is [lo, hi], or a cut's keep × range (8–16 for hypertrophy), the band the volume_adjusted decision names. It is set for MAJOR_GROUPS only.
- The export is one hunk that balanceBlock then calls. M3's volume and scenario tests pass unchanged.
Using it:
- The range is scaled by the week's volumeFactor, so a deload at 0.6 shows 6–12.
- The planned line is plannedHardSets(week, exercises).
- A program with no stored input (a fixture with no generator) shows the planned line only, with 'No stored target for this program'.
- Weeks with no program use today's profile style at factor 1, labelled 'Default for hypertrophy'.
Today's profile never changes a past week's target, which a test proves. The Strength view, the weekly review and the cycle review all read targets.ts.

VIEWS ARE SERVER-RENDERED (problem 1).
Each +page.ts holds a VIEWS map of string-literal relative imports and awaits the requested one on the server and in the browser alike, with no SSR guard:

So the server sends the numbers, summaries, verdicts, table twins and the stored write-up text. No-JS period links work, LCP never waits for a chunk, and nothing shifts at hydration. pnpm budgets counts only the largest awaited view as initial JS.
The price is that every view's CSS is linked as render-blocking. It is measured against each route's CSS allowance, and m6-perf asserts that check-budgets counts it.

THE DETERMINISTIC REVIEW NEVER WAITS FOR THE LLM, AND THE WRITE-UP IS SAFE (problems 11 and 12).
- Creating a review computes, stores and proposes in one transaction, from code alone.
- The write-up is a separate step: agent/reviews/narrate.ts runs one coach turn in the review's own narration thread (entry weekly_review or cycle_review) through M5's composition root, with its launch gate, rate limit and cost cap.
READ-ONLY: runCoachTurn gains toolEffects: ['read'].
- Only read tools are offered.
- Any other call returns is_error 'not available in a review'.
- A mock script that tries to propose proves it.
STORED TEXT: narrative holds the policy-released display text of the run's final display blocks. The page renders the run's display blocks with M5's AnswerBlocks, loaded on demand, over the server-rendered released text.
THREADS: narration threads are filtered by entry. M5's listThreads ('Recent conversations'), the thread-summaries job and memory's other-threads section skip them; reviews reach the coach's memory through coach-review-sources. Tested.
LIFETIME:

slices.title: feat(analytics): tell a real trend from normal variation with a documented robust method
slices.goal: Give dashboards, reviews, the progression rules and the coach one deterministic classifier with four verdicts: real improvement, real decline, normal variation, or not enough data yet, with what is still needed. A single bad session, or a week still in progress, can never make or break a verdict.
newOrChanged:
src/lib/domain/analytics/trend.ts (new): classifyTrend(points, options) returns one of:
- real_trend, with direction and good
- normal_variation
- insufficient_data, with needs {points, days}
Options: direction, mpc {abs?, rel?}, minPoints 6, minSpanDays 21, alpha 0.05. Every result also carries n, spanDays, slopePerWeek, change, changePct, noise, p, outliers[] and the method id 'theil-sen+mann-kendall/1'. Points flagged inProgress are dropped before anything else.

The method:
1. availability
2. a Theil–Sen slope with a median intercept
3. Mann–Kendall S with a two-sided p: exact through Mahonian dynamic programming for n ≤ 20 without ties, otherwise the normal approximation with tie and continuity corrections
4. noise = 1.4826 × the MAD of the residuals
5. real only when p < alpha and |slope × span| ≥ max(MPC, 2 × noise)
Outliers beyond 3 robust SD are flagged, never removed. minPoints is 6 because with n = 4 the smallest two-sided p is 0.083.

openQuestions: Trend thresholds: no verdict before 6 points spanning 21 days, then p < 0.05 and a change of at least the larger of the metric's minimal practical change and twice the noise. The minimal changes are e1RM 2.5 %, weekly volumes 10 %, pace 2 %, load 15 % and adherence 10 points. Confirm these, or name your own.

At 4 weeks there are too few points for a fair verdict. Verdicts at 4w therefore look at the last 12 complete weeks and say so, while the numbers and comparisons cover 4 weeks. Is that right, or should 4w show 'Choose 12 weeks or longer for trends' instead?
Totals and trends cover complete weeks only. The current week shows apart as 'This week so far', compared with the same days of last week. Is that how you want the week in progress shown?

Progress now shows numbers in the units set in your profile, as workout logging does. Before, it used the 'This device' setting. The two differ only if you changed 'This device' alone. Should the device setting win on Progress instead?

Workouts you abandoned or are still logging never count toward PRs, totals or reviews. Their sets still show in an exercise's history and in the start kit's 'prior bests'. Is that right, or should abandoned workouts' sets count as training?

Progression steps, judged over the last 3 sessions:
- about 1 RPE under target in 2 of the 3 → +2.5 %
- lower body → +5 %, only when all 3 agree and the lift is not in a real decline
- at most +5 % a week
- above target → −2.5 % (−5 % when all 3 are above)
- missed reps hold the first time and reduce by 5 % on a repeat
Confirm these as your coaching defaults.
A weekly review becomes available when the week ends, or earlier once every planned session is done or skipped. Do you want the early review, or only after Sunday?

If you decide on next week's changes a few days late, the changes for sessions that have already passed are dropped, and the rest are applied. Accepting from the coach inbox sends you to the review to finish instead. Is that right?

If a cycle review is created late, the weeks you have already lived through become an 'Unplanned' bridge, and the next block and the blocks after it move back. Before a race, the build is shortened instead, so the race date never moves. Is that the behaviour you want?
A next block can only be started from its cycle review, where you choose when it starts. The coach inbox links there and never applies it directly. Confirm.

The coach writes up each review once, when you first open it. That is one read-only coach turn per review, in a conversation hidden from your list. 'Discuss with your coach' starts a separate, visible conversation. Is this acceptable, or should the write-up happen only when you tap 'Ask your coach'?
If you log training after a review, the review says it is out of date. Refresh makes a new revision and keeps the old one, but only while you have not decided on its adjustments. Confirm.
Changing an adjustment means leaving it out or taking a half step. Do you also want to type any amount yourself?

Next-week changes are capped at 12 per review, M5's limit for one proposal. Anything beyond that is listed as 'not proposed', with the reason. Is that acceptable, or should a deload count as one change?
ACWR is shown with a visible caveat, because its link to injury is debated. Should it be shown as planned, hidden behind 'More', or dropped?
Races are taken from best efforts within ±2 % of 5 km, 10 km, half and marathon, plus your reported race results. Should logged runs get an explicit 'race' type instead?
When a program has no outline block left, which is the usual case for general goals with no event, the cycle review appends a new block by the rules. Should it instead suggest building a new program?
The next block can start this week or next Monday. The default is this week when the block ended last Sunday, which leaves no gap. Is that the default you want?
